Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Make Moneo's net worth trustworthy by implementing the agreed design below in full. You are in a dedicated git worktree created from local `main` (which has unpushed commits); work on its branch. Read `AGENTS.md` first and follow it. This Next.js has breaking changes: consult `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing Next-specific code.

Moneo is a local-first, open-source, one-owner personal-finance app. **The target design is written in `docs/net-worth-deep-dive.html` (15 pages). Read all of it first: it is the specification of the finished system.** Where it conflicts with this brief, this brief wins, and update the page.

# Owner's decisions (final)
1. A transfer with one side showing so far: the total is left as is, it's marked unresolved, and earlier days correct themselves when the other side lands. Never assume the other side.
2. Two balances disagreeing on the same date: use the most recently recorded one and tell the owner.
3. Cash machine withdrawal: a card offers to add it to the Cash account; until accepted it counts as money that left. After spending, the owner updates the balance. Cash in a Cash account counts in net worth.
4. A new bank or hand-added item in its first month: its value COUNTS in the net worth total, but the monthly change shows it as its own "newly added" part instead of a gain. The change and percent shown as the month's movement exclude it.
5. Archiving an account: it stays in past days up to the archive date, not removed from all history. If the account still has money, Moneo must ASK what happens to it before archiving: moved to another of the owner's accounts, taken out as cash, or gone. Archiving with money then behaves accordingly and doesn't silently drop net worth without that answer. Keep this small and auditable; use the existing transfer, cash-account and balance tools where they fit, and proposal cards where the app's rules require them.
6. Month change split into money in and out, investments, and newly added. Build this LAST, once transfers are reliable.
7. Other currencies on the graph (#158) stay a known limit. Do not build.
8. Problems: a passing message on Home (`app/home-notices.tsx`); the full persistent list of mismatches and unresolved transfers on Wealth; conflicts on the Home card and detail on Accounts, as in page 11 of the doc.
9. Build in the order below, one step at a time.
10. Do not push. Do not merge. Do not open a PR. The parent merges and pushes later.
Also: returned Scalable withdrawals are shown as if the money simply stayed there, on BOTH the net worth and Scalable charts, with records kept. Money in transit counts as the owner's, once. The owner's €1,000 "Lent to" item is a real loan; don't reclassify any other transaction.

# Findings to fix (from two independent audits; verify in code as you go)
Audit scripts and saved Scalable data for reference only, may contain personal data so never copy them into the repo: `C:\Users\mgsuk\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\3de23844519d7b87\02552df1-ba55-493f-b027-0eb78f9afe1e\scratchpad`.

**Balances and forecast**
- Two snapshots with same date and €1.09 but different source rows count as a conflict (`lib/finance/balances.ts:28,56-58`); strict readers (`lib/finance/review.ts:87`, `lib/finance/model.ts:109`, `app/plan/model-sources.tsx:13`) then return null/unavailable, while Home, Wealth and Accounts use `preferLatestRecorded`. Fix: equal date, currency, amount, and equivalent boundary meaning is agreement; different source IDs alone are not a conflict for date-only closing balances. Don't discard meaningful reviewed-activity or after-transaction boundaries. All readers share one rule. Real conflicts: decision 2.
- Available to spend ignores the opening state: forecast minima are computed after today's events are applied (`lib/finance/calculations.ts:110,137`); €100 plus €1,000 income due today shows €1,100. Include the opening state, and keep current cash distinct from expected end-of-day cash.
- `buildDebtForecast` rejects any non-zero debt whose principal isn't dated today (`lib/finance/wealth.ts:128`), which blocks the whole forecast the next day. Carry forward the last evidenced principal with explicit payment and interest assumptions; ask for an update only when evidence is insufficient.

**Bank data**
- Each sync's balance sits on the last row (`lib/bank/statement.ts:44-45`), so it's lost if that row goes to review or a posting is dated tomorrow. Save the bank's balance as its own observation with the bank's date and balance type. Don't treat available balances as booked; check the Revolut path at `lib/bank/statement.ts:58-61`, where a hold could otherwise count twice.
- A failed import still stamps `last_synced_at` and can clear `last_error` (`workflows/bank-sync.ts:20,96`); an open-sync request failing early is silently ignored (`components/sync-on-open.tsx:8`). Fix both, simply.
- Commerzbank-style banks have no transaction IDs, so overlap rows go to review (`lib/import/match.ts:13-19`). The owner has 14 rows waiting, all repeats of existing ledger rows. Compare occurrence counts of identical rows within a known complete overlap window, counting canonical occurrences rather than accumulated source copies; ambiguous or incomplete windows still go to review. A genuine second identical payment must still land. Provide a safe way for already-waiting exact repeats to be resolved without posting them twice; never delete source records, and keep it audited and undoable where the review system supports that.
- Sync races: refresh protection is a module-local map (`lib/scalable/server.ts:15`); a failed request unconditionally clears tokens even if another request saved a refresh; two syncs can finish in reverse order (`lib/scalable/sync.ts:22`, `supabase/migrations/202611050002_scalable_wealth_sync.sql:8`). Use a small per-connection database claim or version: check whether tokens changed before expiring a login; reject superseded results.
- `Math.max(value, 0)` clamps negative Scalable cash (`lib/scalable/portfolio.ts:52`), and securities are recalculated rather than reconciled to Scalable's total. Preserve signed cash through an appropriate representation (check `wealth_items` constraints; asset amounts must be >= 0 and debts <= 0, so negative cash needs a correct treatment). Report unsupported states explicitly.

**Asset and loan history (`app/money/wealth/net-worth.ts`)**
- `valuationHistory` drops removal events (line ~121), so a position sold and rebought counts during the gap. Treat removal as zero from its date.
- Undoing creation leaves the current item counted in the past; linking a standalone asset to an account filters the linked version out before choosing the latest, so the old standalone value keeps counting (line ~46). Choose the applicable state first, then decide whether it contributes. Distinguish creation undone from a real later removal.
- Loans: a repayment isn't a durable link, so one receipt can reduce several loans, and a voided transaction can be accepted (`lib/finance/iou.ts:64,90`, `lib/ai/iou-proposals.ts:62`, `lib/ai/agent-apply.ts:64,76`). Save an audited repayment association: bank transaction, its financial version, loan, applied amount. Prevent reuse beyond the receipt's amount. Require posted status. Bank corrections or undo require re-review. Date the value change by the bank row, including full settlements.
- The graph has its own simpler balance logic, without reviewed-activity and boundary safeguards (`net-worth.ts:37` vs `balances.ts:65`). Share the boundary rules, and carry uncertainty in historical points so the chart can mark such a day instead of drawing a confident number. Also fix: two same-dated differing snapshots can resolve differently for chart and headline.
- Archived accounts: decision 5 (currently filtered out of all days at `net-worth.ts:36`).
- "Starts where accounts start": `known` currently accepts wealth items alone (`net-worth.ts:81`); the design has the graph start where account data starts. If a workspace has no account data at all, keep a sensible start, and test it.

**Own transfers (the owner's visible problem). This is the core of step 5, so read carefully.**
Facts verified on real data: Scalable lists `kind: cash` rows with `cash.transactionType` DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL; 16 of 43 are returning deposits with ID `RETURN-<withdrawal id>` and the exact opposite amount, with no bank row. A deposit dated 1 Nov was paid by the bank on 2 Nov; a withdrawal dated 24 Aug arrived at the bank on 25 Aug, and that day also had an unrelated equal Revolut receipt, so amount and date alone can false-match. Bank rows for deposits often don't name Scalable ("To invest <name>"), and may carry Scalable's IBAN in `own_account_identifiers`, or be linked or marked as transfers by `lib/finance/own-transfers.ts` (read it: `findOwnTransfers`, `MATCH_DAYS = 3`, `mark_own_named_transfer`, `transfer_id`, `kind='transfer'`). Check what real rows look like with SELECT-only queries (see Safety). Commerzbank-to-Revolut transfers have the same date problem: 7 chart days, e.g. €500 on 15-16 Aug.
Required design:
- Save Scalable's real transfers in their own table once by stable provider ID, with revisions and the `RETURN-` relationship; add new ones at each sync. The recent-activity list is not a complete history; backfill during the history job, and make sure the owner's existing connection backfills after the migration WITHOUT a full chart re-fetch if possible. Records are kept, and reset clears them; handle disconnect consistently with other synced data.
- Do NOT delete returned withdrawals from broker records. Link withdrawal and return. Add a pure read-time step producing a per-day adjustment so the money is counted once and returned withdrawals look as if the money stayed. Apply it to the Home graph, Wealth's month-end table, the Scalable chart, chat, and today's total. Note both Home and Wealth replace today's series point with `currentNetWorth`, so a fix only inside `netWorthSeries` would vanish at today's endpoint. Prefer one function they all call.
- Matching requires opposite principal, same currency, identified accounts proven by IBAN or bank wording (or an existing linked transfer), a unique counterpart within 3 days, and broker activity classified as deposit or withdrawal. Never reuse a leg. Ambiguous or missing sides stay unresolved and visible on Wealth. Transfers to untracked banks stay on their own date. Fees and FX are real changes.
- At the first-sync boundary, apply a correction only for a leg already reflected in the corresponding balance, or the calculated history, first real observation and adjustment could count the same money twice. Test this seam explicitly. Past days before and after first sync must both work.
- Nothing re-runs on new statements: the rule applies at read time. Old prices must not be lost to a re-run; `scalable_value_history` keeps its rows.
- Known outcomes on the owner's data to check at the end with a SELECT-only read-only script: these are the expected corrected values and your acceptance test. 31 Oct €3,524.58; 1 Nov €3,524.58 (was €4,124.58); 2 Nov €3,171.36; 12 Jun €2,629.14 (was €929.14); 15 Jun €2,527.01 (was €827.01); 16 Jun €1,477.08; 23 Jun €968.18; 24 Aug €1,304.89 (was €904.89); 15 Aug €1,562.31 (was €2,062.31); lowest day of the chart 25 Jun €904.56; today €3,175.34 unless real data has moved; month change total -€349.24. Because the owner's DB won't have your migration, run these against a pure in-memory form of the owner's rows you read with SELECT, plus Scalable transfers from the saved audit data, without writing anywhere. Report the actual results for each figure, and investigate any difference rather than adjusting expectations.

**One source and display**
- Today there's `reviews_investigate` net worth in chat (`app/api/chat/route.ts:314`, `lib/finance/review-loader.ts:82`), but no shared current-and-historical source, balance tools include archived accounts (`lib/finance/tools.ts:36`), and artifact cards have no net worth source. Provide one shared deterministic source (totals, past dates, what was left out, freshness) used by Home, Wealth, chat (including past dates), voice and artifacts. Respect existing AI data scopes. Don't add net worth to `scalable_portfolio`, which would count Scalable twice. Update the chat system prompt and app guide if needed.
- Home line when calculated history fails its check; currently only Wealth says so, and only when no days are saved (`app/money/wealth/page.tsx:113`).
- Market move labels: Friday's move is labelled "today" on Sunday (`lib/scalable/sync.ts:29`, `lib/scalable/portfolio.ts:57`, `components/scalable-investments.tsx:44`). Distinguish fetch, inventory and market-price time. Don't backdate current holdings.
- `app/money/wealth/wealth-fields.tsx:20` still says "Only a value dated today counts"; Home's chart label says "at each month end" but it's daily (`app/page.tsx:178`); trade-derived prices include fees (`lib/scalable/history.ts:108-111`): check whether `get_transaction_details` fields are available, and use the fee-free price if that doesn't add a call per trade per run; if it would, say so and keep the simplest correct option.

# The five always-on checks (after each sync; one persistent discrepancy per piece of evidence, never a new warning each sync)
Comparable booked balance observations reconcile to intervening accepted postings. Broker parts reconcile to total. Calculated and observed values meet at a comparable boundary. Transfers have a unique counterpart or explicit unresolved state. Failed imports don't publish success. NOT alarms: negative balances, exact equality with Scalable's returns, a transfer taking more than 3 days (just stays listed). The check on the owner's data today must not produce a false alarm: test against the shapes described.

# Tests that must exist (property-style where practical, not single restated examples)
A matched transfer between tracked accounts is counted once on every day, for any two dates. A returned withdrawal changes nothing. Importing the same row twice leaves every balance reader agreeing. With one currency, today's graph point equals the headline. Home, Wealth and chat agree on the same data. A sell then rebuy is zero during the gap. A loan and its repaid amount don't change net worth. One receipt can't over-settle. The first-sync seam doesn't double count. Unresolved transfers stay visible.

# Order, one commit series per step; run the relevant tests at each
1. Balance conflict rule; available-to-spend; debt forecast.
2. Bank observations; failed-import status; sync coordination; negative Scalable cash; the five checks and where they appear.
3. ID-less bank overlap, and the existing waiting repeats.
4. Asset and loan history, including removal, undo, link, repayment association, archive with the question (decision 5), and cash withdrawal cards (decision 3; check the existing cash flow: `lib/ai/balance-proposals.ts`, `lib/finance/own-transfers.ts`).
5. Scalable transfers, the in-transit step, graph safeguards, and graph start.
6. One shared source for chat, voice and artifacts; Home warning; market dates; wording fixes; then the month split with "newly added" (decisions 4 and 6). Issue #167: comment on it only if asked; don't close it; report what remains.
Finally, update `docs/net-worth-deep-dive.html` so it matches what you actually built and the decisions above: remove #167 and archiving from page 14's limits where solved; add what's on page 8 and page 1 as needed. Keep it final-state only, illustrative numbers only, and fitting its 1600×900 pages. Update README where setup or behaviour changed. Hit every surface in AGENTS.md: pages mobile and desktop, light and dark, chat, voice, artifacts, Home widgets, background jobs, reset, undo, reconnect, disconnect.

# Rules
- Simplest code that works; match nearby style; keep each file's line endings (many are CRLF; on Windows Python `open()` defaults to cp1252, so use UTF-8 and `newline=""` if scripting edits). No new dependencies unless truly necessary. Money is bigint minor units.
- New ordered migrations only; never edit applied ones; keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Migrations run on the owner's real database when the parent applies them later, so each must be safe on existing data, including the existing 642 `scalable_value_history` rows, and additive. Run `node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs` and add SQL regressions in `supabase/tests/` where policies or RPCs change. If a reset function changes, keep everything it did.
- A bug fix starts with a failing test. Commit in steps with plain-language messages, each ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Deferred work goes into GitHub issues via `gh issue create`; don't defer anything in this brief silently. If something can't be done, say so plainly in your report.
- If you need a decision only the owner can make and it changes the design, ask rather than guess. For everything else, decide and report it.

# Safety (strict)
- The Postgres in Docker `moneo-db-1` holds the owner's real financial history. You may read it ONLY with SELECT: `docker exec moneo-db-1 psql -U postgres -d postgres -c "select ..."`. NEVER write to it, apply migrations to it, run `npm run setup` against it, run `docker compose down -v`, or change `.env` secrets. Don't touch `moneo-demo-*`.
- Unit tests mock everything. NEVER call real banks, Scalable or AI services. Use the saved audit data instead of live Scalable. Read-only probes with `withScalable` aren't needed; if you believe one is essential, ask first.
- For browser and SQL testing use a private Docker project of your own on non-default ports (e.g. project name `moneo-nw`, ports 54721/54722), a QA user there (`scripts/e2e-auth.mjs`, `e2e/README.md`), and a test server on a port other than 3000 with `CRON_SECRET` empty. Remove the project, its volumes, copied `.env`, `e2e/.auth.json` and `.qa` afterwards; never commit them. The owner's app runs on port 3000 from `C:\codebases\Moneo`: never stop it, never build in that directory. Only kill processes you started, verified by port and command line, never by name.
- Personal data stays out of the repo (`npm run check:privacy`): no real amounts, names or IBANs in code, tests, docs or commit messages. Your report may contain real figures.
- Screenshots of changed pages in desktop light and mobile dark, using the QA user only; report absolute paths.

# Before finishing
Run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs`, and Playwright specs for changed flows. `e2e/wealth.gated.spec.ts` has a known-stale wording failure tracked in #168; fix it if trivial, since you're changing this page. Quote any failure exactly.

# Final report
Branch and head SHA; commits per step; files changed; exact results of every check; the acceptance table of owner figures (expected vs actual); what the migrations do to existing data and exactly what the parent must run after merging, including anything needed to backfill Scalable transfers and whether it makes real Scalable calls; decisions you made; anything not done, deferred or unverified (with issue numbers); screenshots. Do not claim anything you did not run.
I'll read the spec and the relevant code, then implement the six steps in order, committing and testing each one.

 Moneo · open-source personal finance · deep dive

=====SECTION class="scene" data-title="The idea" data-short="Idea">
 The idea 
 Everything you own, minus everything you owe 
 Code adds it up from your records, in whole cents. The AI can explain the number; code produces it. 
 Accounts € 2,550 Bank accounts and cash you told Moneo about. 
 Investments € 3,200 Scalable holdings and cash, plus investments you add by hand.

 Never a silent guess An unknown input is left out and named. If two balances conflict, Moneo uses the most recently recorded one and tells you. 
 History stays Corrections add to the record. Source rows and earlier versions are kept, and changes can be undone. 
 One question, one calculation: what can the records prove on this date? 
=====SECTION class="scene" data-title="Where the numbers come from" data-short="Evidence">
 The evidence 
 Five kinds of evidence, each with one job 
 Each keeps its own date and source, so any figure can be traced back to what produced it. 
 Record Comes from What it proves 
 Transactions Statements, bank sync, you Money moved on this date. Only posted rows count, so pending card payments never change the balance. 
 Balance observations Bank sync, statements, you This balance was stated on this date, by the bank, a statement or you. Each is saved with its own date and type. 
 Dated values Scalable sync, you This holding or asset was worth this much on this date, including when it was removed. 
 Scalable transfers Scalable, once per transfer Money moved in or out of the broker. Each one has Scalable's own ID, and returned withdrawals stay linked to their return. 
 Calculated history Worked out by Moneo Your portfolio's value on days before its first sync. Kept apart from real records and labelled as calculated. 
 Recorded facts and calculated values are stored apart, and calculated days are labelled. 
=====SECTION class="scene" data-title="The number today" data-short="Today">
 Today's number 
 Last known balance, plus what happened since 
 An account's balance is its latest balance observation, moved by every posted transaction after it. 
 Mon Bank says € 2,600.00 balance observation 
 Tue Posted -€ 40.00 groceries 
 Wed Posted -€ 10.00 phone bill 
 Wed Pending -€ 25.00 card hold, not counted until it posts 
 Today Balance € 2,550.00 
 Older values Stay counted, and say so A value from Friday still counts on Sunday. Wealth names it as not from today, so a late sync never makes money vanish. 
 Future dates Don't count yet A value dated in the future stays out and is named as not counted. 
 Agreeing records Two sources, one fact The same date and amount, describing the same point in the day, is agreement. Different amounts are a conflict: Moneo uses the most recently recorded one and tells you. 
=====SECTION class="scene" data-title="Every day on the graph" data-short="Graph">
 The graph 
 Each past day is worked out the same way 
 The graph uses the same balance rules as the headline, so it isn't surer of a past day than the records are. 
 Step 1 Accounts Latest observation on or before that day, moved by later postings. Earlier days are worked back from the first one. 
 → 
 Step 2 Values The value in force that day: nothing before it existed, and zero once sold or removed. An undone addition never counted.

 Step 3 Portfolio Before Scalable's first real sync, the calculated value. From that sync on, only real ones. 
 →

 Starts where accounts start Values alone would look like a jump when bank history begins. The Scalable chart on Wealth goes back further.

 Home's daily graph and Wealth's month-end table read the same points. 
=====SECTION class="scene" data-title="Moving your own money" data-short="Transfers">
 Own transfers 
 Moving your own money doesn't change what you own 
 The two sides of a transfer between your tracked accounts often land on different days. Money in transit counts as yours, once. 
 Money in transit 
 €500 from your bank to Scalable 
 Mon Tue Wed 
 Bank 3,000 2,500 2,500 
 Scalable 1,500 1,500 1,500 
 Overlap removed -500 0 0 
 Net worth 4,000 4,000 4,000 
 Scalable records it on Monday, and the bank pays on Tuesday. Until the bank side arrives, today's total can run high by that amount, and the transfer shows as unresolved. Once it lands, Monday corrects itself. No record is rewritten.

 A withdrawal bounces back 
 Mon Tue Wed 
 Scalable's records 1,000 500 1,000 
 On the way back 0 +500 0 
 Shown on both charts 1,000 1,000 1,000

 Other banks, fees, currency A transfer to a bank Moneo doesn't track leaves net worth on its own date. Fees and exchange-rate differences are real changes.

 Investments 
 Replaying your history from your first trade 
 Each sync records today's real value. For earlier days, Moneo replays your transactions and past prices in the background until one run passes. 
 Read Every transaction Settled trades and cash moves, each counted once. Read-only tools only.

 Matching today proves where the replay ends, and the first real sync tests one more point. Days in between stay labelled as calculated.

 Life cycle 
 Each thing you own counts only while you own it 
 Past days use the state that was true then. Undo and archiving are the deliberate exceptions. 
 What happens Effect How Moneo treats it 
 You sell, then rebuy later Shares count as zero in between The sale cash counts in between, and the shares don't, so nothing counts twice.

 Staying up to date 
 Old numbers first, fresh numbers when they land 
 Opening Moneo never waits on a bank. The page shows what's saved, then updates by itself once a sync finishes. 
 When you open it Sync on open and return Scalable at most every 15 minutes, and each bank at most hourly, because you're present. 
 In the background Hourly job, about once a day each Catches up after the computer was asleep. Scalable runs if its values aren't from today. 
 Per connection Syncs don't clash Each connection is claimed in the database, one at a time. An older result can't overwrite a newer one, and a renewed login token can't be used twice. 
 Bank data you can trust 
 The bank's balance is saved even when no new transaction arrives

 A sync only counts when it landed

 A failed import never shows as a successful sync 
 A request that fails before reaching the bank is reported too

 Trust 
 The numbers keep checking each other 
 After each sync, Moneo compares independent records. Each piece of evidence raises one notice, not a new one each sync. 
 Bank adds up Two balance observations of the same type, at a clear point in the day, differ by exactly the postings between them. 
 Scalable adds up Holdings, crypto and cash add up to Scalable's own total. 
 History meets reality The last calculated day is compared with the first real sync. 
 Transfers pair up Every own transfer has one other side, or is shown as unresolved. 
 Imports landed A failed import can't publish a successful status. 
 Guaranteed by automated tests

 Importing the same row twice leaves every balance agreeing 
 With one currency, today's point equals the headline 
 Home, Wealth and chat agree on the same data 
 A loan and its repaid amount don't change net worth 
 Deliberately not alarms 
 Negative balances: an overdraft or a fee can be real 
 Exact match with Scalable's returns: its periods and rounding differ 
 A transfer taking longer than 3 days: weekends and reversals happen, so it stays listed as unresolved, without an alarm 
=====SECTION class="scene" data-title="When something is wrong" data-short="Problems">
 Problems 
 A clean page, and nothing hidden 
 Passing issues come and go in the corner. Problems that change the number stay on it until they are fixed. 
 Problem On Home Where the detail stays 
 A value isn't from today Passing message, once per change Wealth names each item and its date 
 A sync failed or a login ended Passing message, once per change Settings shows the connection and what to do 
 Something can't be counted On the card, until fixed "Not counted" names the item

 Every screen 
 One calculation, wherever you ask 
 Screens read the total from one source. The AI quotes that total, and can only do further sums on top of it. 
 One source Net worth calculation Current and past totals, what was left out, and how fresh each input is. 
 Home Headline and graph 
 Wealth Totals and tables 
 Chat Any date you ask about 
 Voice The same figures

 This month Split in two Money in and out, and investments, so spending and markets are kept apart. Moving your own money is neither. 
 Available to spend Only money you have Starts from your opening cash, not income that is only expected. The plan uses the same balance rules. 
 Debts Keep forecasting A debt's last known amount carries forward, with its payments. It asks for an update only when the evidence runs out.

 Decisions 
 What we chose, and why 
 Chose Instead of Because 
 Money in transit is yours Letting it dip or double A transfer isn't a gain or a loss. Past the 3-day window it stays visible as unresolved

 Limits 
 What Moneo can't know, and where to read the code

 Known limits 
 Money you never recorded isn't counted, and purchases count as spent even if they keep their value 
 Cash you spend only changes when you update the balance
